transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm not wasting your time. 

I guess I'm here because I've been having a little trouble with my eating habits lately. Nothing too terrible, I hope, but... well, I take this evening class, and afterwards I sometimes stop for food on the way back. And I guess I just end up eating a bit much. I'll have a full fast-food meal, and then maybe grab some candy from the vending machine, and then when I get home I just keep having more snacks. 

It's almost like I'm trying to make up for the whole day all at once, if that makes sense? I know I shouldn't do it, and I really do try to be good during the day, but it just sort of gets away from me. Is that... is that the sort of thing you handle here? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Do you usually feel guilty after these late-night eating episodes?

Guilty? Oh, um... I don't know if I'd use the word guilty, exactly. I haven't really thought about it like that. 

I mean, I know it's probably not the smartest habit, especially since I just sit at a desk doing bookkeeping all day, but... I don't really beat myself up over it, I don't think. I mostly just feel a bit, well, overly full. And maybe just a little silly for letting it get away from me again. But I try to just stay positive and tell myself I'll be better the next day. 

I hope that's an okay way to handle it? I just try not to make too big a fuss over things, you know?
Do you usually feel hungry before these late-night eating episodes?

Hungry? Oh, um... you know, I haven't really paid much attention to that. I guess... probably not? 

I mean, it's not like my stomach is growling or I'm completely starving or anything. It's more just... I get out of my class, and the food is right there on the drive home, and it just seems like a nice way to wind down. I hope that doesn't sound too foolish. I just sort of start snacking without really checking if my body actually needs the food first. 

Is that... does that make sense to you? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
How often do these late-night eating episodes happen?

How often? Oh, well... I suppose it's been going on for about the past three months. Usually, it's just, oh, at least one night each week after my class. 

But, um... there is something else I probably ought to mention. I really hope you won't judge me too harshly for this, I know it's not very dignified for a man my age... but when I overeat like that, sometimes I... well, I make myself throw up afterward. Just to get rid of that uncomfortable feeling, you know? 

It's not every single day, just that one night a week usually. I hope it's okay that I'm sharing that with you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details, and I hope you don't think too badly of me for it.
Do you feel like you have control over whether or not you eat this way on those late nights?

Control? Oh, well... I really wish I could say I do. I know a man my age ought to have better discipline, and I hope you don't think too poorly of me, but... no, not really. 

Once I start on those snacks, I'll keep telling myself in my head to just close the bag and go to bed. I really do try to reason with myself. But... it's like my hands just keep reaching for more anyway. I just keep going until I feel completely embarrassed and, well, a bit sick of myself for not stopping. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound too weak-willed to you? I really do try to be good, it just... gets away from me sometimes. I hope I'm explaining this okay for your notes.
How often do you make yourself throw up after eating?

Oh, um... yes, I think I might have touched on that just a moment ago, but I want to make sure I'm answering you properly. It's really just tied to those same nights. 

So, for about the past three months, it's usually just that one night each week after my class. Whenever I overeat like that, I... well, I make myself sick right after. I really do try to keep it contained, so it's just that once a week, not every day or anything. 

I hope I'm being clear enough for you? I know I'm probably repeating myself a bit, I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need for your notes without being too much of a bother.
Do you usually feel stressed, anxious, or upset before these late-night eating episodes?

Stressed? Oh, um... well, I hope this isn't an unhelpful answer, but... I don't really think so. 

I mean, my work doing the books can get a little tedious during the day, sure, but I wouldn't say I'm particularly anxious or upset when I get home. It's more just... I don't know, a bad habit that I fall into once I finally sit down after my class. I don't really notice any strong emotions right before it starts. 

I hope that's okay? I know sometimes there's supposed to be a deeper reason for these sorts of things, and I don't want to give you the wrong impression or make your job harder... I just haven't really noticed feeling upset beforehand. Does that make sense for your notes, or did you mean something else?
Do you think eating helps you feel better when you're not even hungry?

Feel better? Um... well, I suppose since I'm not really feeling upset to begin with, it doesn't exactly make me feel *better*, if that makes sense? 

I mean, I'm not really eating to comfort myself or anything like that. I know some people eat when they're sad, and I don't want to sound like I'm doing that... it's just, well, like I said, it just kind of happens. I don't feel a big sense of relief or anything while I'm doing it. Honestly, it's mostly just... embarrassing afterward. 

I hope that answers your question alright? I'm sorry if I'm not giving you the kind of answers you usually get for this sort of thing. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
How many times do you make yourself throw up in a typical month?

Oh, um... well, I know we just talked about this a little bit, and I really hope I'm not confusing things for you. 

Since it's, you know, just that one night a week after my class... I guess in a typical month, that would make it about four times? Maybe five, depending on how the weeks fall in the month. It's been like that for the past three months or so. Just the one night a week where I overeat and then have to... well, make myself sick. 

I try very hard to keep it just to that, so it's not getting out of hand or anything. Does four times a month sound like what you need for your paperwork? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right numbers so I don't mess up your assessment.
Do you ever feel like eating helps you avoid thinking about problems or stressful situations?

Well, um... I really hope I'm not being difficult by saying this, but... no, not really. I don't think I'm using it to avoid anything. 

My life is pretty quiet, you know? The bookkeeping keeps me busy during the day, but it's not exactly high-stress, and I don't really have any major problems I'm trying to hide from. I'm definitely not trying to block things out or run away from anything... it really is just that silly routine I get stuck in on that one night. 

I'm sorry, I know it would probably make a lot more sense if I had some big stressful situation I was trying to cope with. I feel like I'm probably not fitting the usual pattern for this kind of thing. I hope it's okay that I don't have a better reason for it? Am I giving you enough to work with for your evaluation?
Do you feel like there's something that triggers your desire to eat on those late nights after class?

Um... well, I've thought about that, because I know there's usually supposed to be a reason, right? Like a trigger or something. But honestly... no, I don't think there's anything specific that sets it off. 

It's just that one night a week, and it's always the same. I get home from class, and it's late, and the house is quiet... and it just sort of happens. I don't feel particularly upset or triggered by anything that happened in class or at work that day. It's almost just like a bad habit I've fallen into, you know? 

I really hope that's an okay answer. I know it probably doesn't help you figure out the root cause or anything. I'm sorry I don't have a clearer explanation for it. Does that make sense, though? That it just feels like a routine rather than something being triggered?
Do you ever have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short time without making yourself throw up afterward?

Oh, um... no. No, I always make sure to... take care of it afterward. 

I know it sounds awful, and I'm really sorry if it's disappointing to hear, but if I eat all that food, I just... I couldn't just leave it there. I'd feel too terrible about myself. So, no, it's always followed by... you know, getting rid of it. 

I try to make sure I'm doing it right away so I don't gain weight or cause any other problems. I really don't want to be a burden on anyone's health system by letting myself get completely out of shape. Is it... is it bad that I always do it? I mean, I know the whole thing isn't great, but I hope I'm at least giving you clear answers for your notes. I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Do you ever have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short time without making yourself throw up afterward, other than the nights after your class?

Um... no, definitely not. It really is just that one night a week. 

I'm pretty good about sticking to my normal meals the rest of the time. I don't really have the urge to eat like that on any other day. I try to keep things very orderly, you know? Just... regular meals, sensible portions. I'd never want to let myself get completely out of control all the time. 

So it's just the one night. I hope that's... I hope that's what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are. I'm not trying to hide anything else, I promise. Is that... is that helpful for your evaluation?
Do you ever feel a loss of control during these episodes of eating large amounts of food?

Well, um... I guess I wouldn't want to say I completely lose my mind or anything, because I really do try to be a disciplined person. But... yes, I suppose I do lose control a bit. 

It's just... once I start on those snacks, I keep telling myself in my head to just close the bag and go to bed. I know I should. But my hands just keep reaching for more, almost on their own, until I feel really embarrassed and... well, sick of myself. 

I really hate admitting that, I'm sorry. I hope that doesn't make me sound too weak or terrible? I'm just trying to give you the honest truth so you have exactly what you need. Did I explain that okay?
Do you think making yourself throw up after eating is a way of punishing yourself for overeating?

Oh, um... punishing myself? I... I don't think I'd call it that. I really hope I'm not making things complicated by saying this, but I don't think I'm trying to be mean to myself on purpose. 

It's more just... well, almost like balancing a ledger at work, I guess. I made a mistake by eating all those things, and I just need to... to correct the error. Just to undo it so I don't gain weight and let myself go. I just want to fix it so everything is back to normal and I'm not a bother to anyone. 

Does that make sense? I'm sorry if that's not the answer you were expecting... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea. I'm definitely not trying to hurt myself, I promise. I just like to keep things orderly. Is that an okay way to explain it?
Do you ever have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short time without making yourself throw up afterward, at any time other than the nights after your class?

Oh, um... I'm sorry, I think you might have asked me about this just a little bit ago? Maybe I wasn't clear enough the first time—my apologies if I confused you, I really don't want to make your job harder. 

But no, definitely not at any other time. Like I was saying earlier, I really try to keep my meals very structured and sensible the rest of the week. I promise it's strictly just that one night after my class. I wouldn't want you to think I'm completely out of control every single day, because I really do try my best to be good. 

Did I... did I answer it better this time? I just want to make sure you have everything you need for your notes.
Do you ever use other methods, such as excessive exercise, laxatives, or fasting, to try to compensate for the calories you consumed during these episodes?

Oh, um... no, no I don't do anything like that. I hope that's the right answer? 

I really don't use laxatives or... or try to starve myself or anything extreme. I try to be very reasonable about things. I mean, I might try to eat just a little bit lighter the next day, you know, maybe have a salad for lunch instead of a sandwich, just to balance the books, so to speak. But I definitely don't go days without eating or spend hours on a treadmill. I'm not... I'm not doing anything dangerous, I promise. 

I just want to make sure I'm doing things the right way. Does that sound okay to you? I hope I'm not giving you the impression that I'm completely reckless with my health.
Do you feel that your eating behavior and subsequent purging are linked to concerns about your weight or body shape?

Oh, um... well, I suppose so, yes. I hope it's alright to admit that. I mean, I don't obsess over it every single second of the day, I really don't. But... well, on days when my shirt feels a little tight around my middle, it just... it really bothers me. 

It makes me feel like I've failed, you know? Like I haven't been the careful, disciplined person I always try so hard to be. It's silly, I know, because the rest of my bookkeeping work might be perfectly fine that day, but I just feel so... sloppy, I guess. And I really hate feeling like I'm letting myself go. 

I just want to present a neat, tidy appearance so I'm not an eyesore to anyone. Is it normal to feel that way? I hope I don't sound terribly vain or anything. I just like things to be orderly, even myself. Does that make sense?
Do you ever have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short time without feeling like you need to make yourself throw up afterward?

Oh, gosh... I'm so sorry, I feel like I might be repeating myself, which probably means I didn't explain it properly just a moment ago. Please forgive me, I really don't mean to make you ask things twice. 

But no, I don't ever have times where I eat a lot like that and *don't* feel the need to... well, take care of it afterward. If I ever slip up and have that large amount of food, the urge to... to undo it, I guess, is always there. I wouldn't just eat all that and sit with it without fixing the situation. That would feel so irresponsible, and I really do try my best to be a responsible person in every other part of my life. 

I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the exact right information so your records are perfectly accurate.
